skill.name: code-review-excellence
skill.description: Guides AI assistants through structured code reviews that identify bugs, security risks, test gaps, and maintainable feedback.
skill.summary: Guide systematic pull request reviews with constructive, prioritized feedback.

No additional semantic security findings were identified.

content.value_statement: Code reviews can become slow, inconsistent, or too personal. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a structured way to deliver clear, useful PR feedback.
actual_capabilities: Structures reviews into context, design, line-level analysis, and final decision phases.
Provides review checklists for security, performance, testing, and maintainability.
Suggests constructive feedback language with blocking, suggestion, nit, learning, and praise labels.
Highlights common Python, TypeScript, and JavaScript review issues.
Includes a pull request review summary template for consistent reviewer output.
limitations: It does not inspect repositories or pull requests by itself.
It depends on the assistant having access to the relevant diff and project context.
Referenced resource files and scripts are named in the guide but are not included in this package.
It gives review guidance, not formal security certification or legal compliance approval.

use_cases.title: Review a Feature Pull Request
use_cases.description: Apply a repeatable review flow to check correctness, security, tests, and maintainability before merge.

use_cases.title: Coach New Reviewers
use_cases.description: Teach developers how to write specific, prioritized, and respectful feedback during code review.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Review Quality
use_cases.description: Create shared expectations for when to approve, comment, request changes, or escalate architectural concerns.

prompt_templates.title: Basic PR Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a small pull request
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this pull request using the code-review-excellence skill. Focus on correctness, test coverage, and clear feedback. Separate blocking issues from suggestions.

prompt_templates.title: Security-Focused Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review for risky application changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the security review checklist from this skill. Look for input validation, authorization, secret handling, injection risks, and sensitive data exposure. Explain each concern with severity.

prompt_templates.title: Mentoring Review Feedback
prompt_templates.scenario: Review that should help a less experienced developer learn
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this change with constructive mentoring feedback. Ask useful questions, explain tradeoffs, and mark comments as blocking, important, nit, suggestion, learning, or praise.

prompt_templates.title: Architecture and Test Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of a large or design-heavy change
prompt_templates.prompt: Perform a staged architecture and test-quality review. Evaluate design fit, alternatives, rollout risk, test behavior, edge cases, and maintainability. End with a clear merge recommendation.

output_examples.input: A small pull request adds an API endpoint and basic tests.
output_examples.output: The review lists one blocking authorization concern, two test suggestions, and a concise approval path after the required fix.

output_examples.input: A junior developer requests feedback on a refactor.
output_examples.output: The response uses question-based comments, explains maintainability tradeoffs, praises the simplified flow, and separates learning notes from required changes.

output_examples.input: A large feature changes data access and user-facing behavior.
output_examples.output: The review starts with design risks, checks edge cases and performance, recommends smaller staged follow-up reviews, and gives a clear request-changes verdict.

best_practices: Provide the assistant with the pull request description, diff, tests, and relevant design context.
Ask for prioritized feedback so blocking issues stay separate from optional improvements.
Use the final review template to make strengths, required changes, questions, and verdict easy to scan.
anti_patterns: Do not use the skill to enforce personal style choices that linters should handle.
Do not request a final approval when the assistant has not seen the relevant code or tests.
Do not mix minor suggestions with blocking issues without clear severity labels.

faq.question: Does this skill review code automatically?
faq.answer: No. It guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code after you provide the pull request, diff, or code context.

faq.question: Can it find security issues?
faq.answer: It includes security review checklists, but results depend on the code context provided to the assistant.

faq.question: Is it useful for junior developers?
faq.answer: Yes. It emphasizes constructive questions, clear severity labels, and explanations that support learning.

faq.question: Which languages does it cover?
faq.answer: It includes examples for Python, TypeScript, and JavaScript, plus general review practices for other languages.

faq.question: Can teams adapt the review template?
faq.answer: Yes. Teams can reuse the summary, strengths, required changes, suggestions, questions, and verdict structure.

faq.question: Does it replace CI, linters, or security scanners?
faq.answer: No. It recommends using automation for formatting, linting, tests, and scans before human review.
